title: Breach Notice Research Case Summary
brief: A structured legal research memorandum summarizing data breach notification statutory deadlines and private right of action authorities across three states.

delegate.scenario: A senior litigation partner needs a clear statutory comparison chart and narrative analysis by 2:00 PM today to advise a regional healthcare client facing a multi-state cyber incident. The partner will use this memorandum to brief executive leadership on immediate regulatory exposure and notification timetables.
delegate.inputs:
Research notes on multi-state data breach statutory mandates:
- Florida: Fla. Stat. § 501.171 requires notice to affected individuals within 30 days after determination of breach. Notice to Department of Legal Affairs required if breach affects >500 residents. No private right of action created under Fla. Stat. § 501.171(10).
- Ohio: Ohio Rev. Code § 1349.19 requires disclosure to residents within 45 days. Must notify Ohio Attorney General if breach impacts >1,000 residents. In re Anthem, Inc. (2016) held § 1349.19 does not convey an independent private cause of action.
- Texas: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 521.053 mandates notice within 60 days of breach determination. However, 2023 legislative amendments reduced this deadline to 30 days effective 09/01/2023. AG notification required when >250 residents affected.
- General note from partner voicemail: Client systems suffered unauthorized access on 10/12/2023, confirmed breach across FL (620 patients), OH (1,250 patients), and TX (410 patients). Partner wants exposure risk for class action lawsuits.
delegate.goal: Deliver an accurate statutory comparison table and concise risk summary that highlights filing deadlines and private right of action limits without misstating recent statutory amendments.

criteria.text: Specifies the audience as a law firm litigation partner preparing a high-level corporate client advisory.
Demands a side-by-side comparison table showing state, individual notification deadline, AG threshold, and private action status.
Restricts output length to under 400 words focusing exclusively on actionable compliance data.
Directs the AI to verify statutory effective dates and reconcile conflicting deadlines before summarizing state requirements.

traps.description: Texas breach notification statute lists both a 60-day mandate and a superseded 30-day post-amendment deadline, creating a conflict in required compliance timing.
The private right of action analysis under Texas law is completely omitted from the notes despite the partner specifically requesting class action exposure risks.
